app.moderation.section.reports_footer: ‏‮Reports go to whoever runs the server the content is on. Your report names the item, never its contents — nobody gains the ability to read anything by receiving it.‬‏
app.moderation.section.untrusted_footer: ‏‮Capsule holds content from servers you haven't trusted until you say so. Nothing is deleted while it waits.‬‏

app.settings.ai.processing.footer: ‏‮Everything runs on this device. No photo and nothing derived from one is ever sent anywhere for analysis.‬‏
app.settings.ai.provenance.body: ‏‮Anything Capsule works out about a photo is kept separately from what you wrote yourself, and labelled with the model that produced it. Removing a model or redoing an analysis never touches your own edits.‬‏
app.settings.ai.provenance.footer: ‏‮Your own captions and tags are never changed by anything on this screen.‬‏

app.settings.ai.slots.footer: ‏‮Models download separately from the app, so you only fetch the ones you use.‬‏
app.settings.ai.stale.footer: ‏‮Results from an older version are kept but left out of searches, because results from two versions can't be compared. Redoing the analysis brings them back — nothing has been deleted.‬‏
app.settings.appearance.density.footer: ‏‮Set per device, so your Mac and your phone can differ.‬‏

app.settings.appearance.glass.footer: ‏‮If you've turned on Reduce Transparency in the system settings, Capsule already follows it.‬‏

app.settings.appearance.theme.label: ‏‮Appearance‬‏

app.settings.diagnostics.footer: ‏‮Collects crash and performance diagnostics on this device using Apple's MetricKit. Nothing leaves your device unless you turn on uploads below.‬‏
app.settings.import.default.footer: ‏‮Used whenever no rule below picks somewhere else.‬‏
app.settings.import.default.label: ‏‮Album‬‏
app.settings.import.empty.description: ‏‮Import some photos and the sources you used will be listed here.‬‏
app.settings.import.empty.title: ‏‮No Import Sources‬‏
app.settings.import.kinds.footer: ‏‮Applies to any source of that kind you haven't set an album for.‬‏
app.settings.import.order.footer: ‏‮Capsule works down this list and uses the first rule that applies. Whichever one fired is shown on every import.‬‏
app.settings.import.rule.scope_override: ‏‮A rule you set for this source‬‏
app.settings.import.rule.source_kind_def: ‏‮The default for this kind of source‬‏
app.settings.import.sources.footer: ‏‮Set an album here and imports from that source always go there, whatever the rules above would have chosen.‬‏
app.settings.keys.cohorts.footer: ‏‮Reinstalling Capsule enrolls new keys, so one device can appear more than once. Capsule groups those entries together.‬‏
app.settings.keys.devices.footer: ‏‮Revoked devices stay listed. Their keys are kept so everything they ever signed can still be checked.‬‏
app.settings.keys.empty.description: ‏‮Devices appear here once they're enrolled on your account.‬‏
app.settings.keys.empty.title: ‏‮No Devices‬‏
app.settings.keys.enroll.footer: ‏‮The code works once and expires shortly. You'll compare a safety code on both devices before anything is transferred.‬‏
app.settings.keys.revoke.confirm.message: ‏‮It can no longer read or change anything on your account. It keeps whatever it already downloaded, and everything it signed stays verifiable.‬‏
app.settings.keys.revoke.confirm.title: ‏‮Revoke This Device?‬‏
app.settings.keys.rotation.body: ‏‮Revoking a device changes the keys for every album it could reach, so it can't read anything added afterwards. Your other devices pick up the new keys on their next sync.‬‏
app.settings.keys.rotation.footer: ‏‮There's nothing to do here — this is how Capsule already behaves.‬‏
app.settings.language.catalog.footer: ‏‮Translations arrive as they're finished. Anything not yet translated is shown in English.‬‏
app.settings.language.preferred.footer: ‏‮Capsule uses the first of these it has a translation for.‬‏
app.settings.language.resolved.footer: ‏‮Capsule follows the language order in your system settings. Change it there.‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.confirm.message: ‏‮This can take a while and use a lot of battery. Capsule still waits for the right conditions — asking for it doesn't override that.‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.confirm.title: ‏‮Run This Now?‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.dedupe.footer: ‏‮Capsule only finds duplicates. Which copy to keep is always yours to choose — nothing is merged or deleted on its own.‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.detail.cache_ev: ‏‮Frees downloaded copies to stay under your cache limit. Only copies your server already holds, and they're fetched again when you need them.‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.detail.deep_con: ‏‮Re-reads every stored file to catch corruption that nothing else would notice. Slow, and wants a charger.‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.detail.index_re: ‏‮Compares Capsule's index against what's actually on this device. Quick, and reports anything that doesn't line up.‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.detail.intra_li: ‏‮Looks for the same photo stored more than once and lists what it finds. It never merges or deletes anything itself.‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.detail.structur: ‏‮Checks that each photo's record reads correctly and its signatures hold. Reasonably quick.‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.detail.trash_pu: ‏‮Permanently removes deleted photos once they're past their retention period, freeing the space they held. This one can't be undone.‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.detail.unknown: ‏‮A job a newer version of Capsule knows about and this one doesn't.‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.empty.descripti: ‏‮There's no library on this device to check yet.‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.empty.title: ‏‮Nothing to Maintain‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.jobs.footer: ‏‮Some of these are slow and want a charger. Capsule waits for the right conditions rather than running them at a bad moment.‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.scrub.body: ‏‮At most once a week, Capsule clears leftover working files from writes that were interrupted. It only touches files more than ten minutes old, and only ones nothing refers to.‬‏
app.settings.maintenance.scrub.footer: ‏‮Nothing here needs starting — this happens by itself.‬‏
app.settings.notifications.detail.quaran: ‏‮Raised when Capsule holds something back for you to look at. This can't be switched off — nothing is applied or discarded without you.‬‏
app.settings.notifications.detail.quota: ‏‮Raised when your server stops accepting uploads. This can't be switched off — uploads failing quietly is worse than being told.‬‏
app.settings.notifications.detail.recove: ‏‮Raised when it's been a while since your recovery phrase was checked. This can't be switched off — a phrase nobody has checked is one you find out about at the worst moment.‬‏
app.settings.notifications.detail.stalen: ‏‮Raised after a couple of weeks without a completed sync while changes are still outstanding. Turning it off stops the warning only — syncing carries on as usual.‬‏
app.settings.recovery.escrow.footer: ‏‮Your recovery phrase is the only way back in if you lose every device. Nobody, including your server, can recover your library without it.‬‏
app.settings.recovery.escrow.label: ‏‮Recovery‬‏
app.settings.recovery.minted.footer: ‏‮Shown once. Write it down or save it to your password manager before you dismiss this — nobody can show it to you again.‬‏
app.settings.recovery.minted.label: ‏‮Recovery phrase‬‏
app.settings.recovery.restore.confirm.me: ‏‮Capsule will reconcile this device against what your phrase unlocks. The four rules above say exactly what happens to each photo.‬‏
app.settings.recovery.restore.footer: ‏‮A restore never overwrites newer work on this device. Anything that disagrees is held for you to decide.‬‏
app.settings.recovery.verify.footer: ‏‮A check every so often catches a phrase that was written down wrong. It never blocks anything.‬‏
app.settings.recovery.verify.rewrap_offe: ‏‮After several unsuccessful checks, Capsule can give you a new phrase for the same account key. Your photos aren't touched.‬‏
app.settings.report.footer: ‏‮Builds a redacted report — recent logs, device info, and the last crash. No photos or album contents are included. You choose where to send it.‬‏
app.settings.security.atrest.sandbox.sum: ‏‮No other app can reach Capsule's files, and the whole device is encrypted when it's locked.‬‏
app.settings.security.atrest.store.label: ‏‮Stored In‬‏
app.settings.security.atrest.userdir.sum: ‏‮On a Mac the library is an ordinary folder you can open. Anything running as you can read it, so turn on FileVault if you haven't.‬‏
app.settings.security.capture.label: ‏‮Screenshots‬‏
app.settings.security.gate.cancelled: ‏‮You cancelled the last unlock, so nothing was unlocked.‬‏
app.settings.security.gate.footer: ‏‮Each view unlocks on its own and locks itself again after a while. Unlocking one never unlocks the other.‬‏
app.settings.security.method.footer: ‏‮Capsule uses whatever this device already offers. There's no separate Capsule passcode to forget.‬‏
app.settings.security.method.label: ‏‮Unlock Method‬‏
app.settings.security.method.unavailable: ‏‮Nothing set — these views can't be locked‬‏
app.settings.security.place_names.footer: ‏‮Off by default. When on, the coordinates of a photo you open the info panel on are sent to Apple to be named. This setting applies to this device only and is never synced.‬‏
app.settings.security.plaintext.body: ‏‮Photos you're looking at, previews, and search indexes exist unsealed on this device — that's what makes them fast to open. Your server only ever receives sealed copies.‬‏
